reviewer: Codex with isolated medium correctness reviewer

claims.summary: For an unsatisfiable Boolean multilinear clustered system on v variables, background Q, overlap L, local satisfiability through s clusters and respectful expansion (s,delta,xi), the certificate C=(delta*s-2xi)/(2L) is <=v/3-xi/(2L) when integer s>=2 and <=w/2-xi/(2L) when s=1, with w bounding input support. Thus a positive certificate additionally requiring w<=C is <=v/3; bounded-width CNF certificates also cannot reach half the variable count.
claims.assessment: Working all-field certificate-parameter ceiling, passed by the sole medium reviewer. Minimal unsatisfiable core excludes globally private respectful neighbours; hypergeometric singleton probability is <=2/3; overlap counts nonempty variable clusters. Singleton range is controlled separately by one nonzero input. Bounds the published numerical certificate, never actual PC degree from above; zero-slack corollary uses its local-satisfiability conclusion.
claims.rationale: Rules out obtaining the moving near-half-variable sufficient window by optimizing the checked respectful-expansion certificate, even with regrouping and overlap. No novelty or general lower-bound impossibility is claimed.

claims.summary: For an unsatisfiable Boolean system with v incidence columns, row widths<=w, boundary expansion c through positive integer R, and common Boolean-function immunity nu, every positive certificate B=R(nu/4-(w-c)) is <=v/4. The added applicability condition w<=B cannot enlarge the bound.
claims.assessment: Working elementary parameter proof. Immunity and expansion imply R<m for an unsatisfiable system by private-variable peeling; then cR<=v, nu<=w and c<=w bound the certificate. Semantic consequences are nonzero multilinear Boolean polynomials, not arbitrary formal polynomials. The stronger assignment-indicator Rc/2 criterion is separately covered by the respectful ceiling, not by the quarter bound.
claims.rationale: Calibrates a second major published old-degree criterion against the current moving-cutoff target. It does not bound actual PC hardness, reject other immunity arguments, or claim literature-wide optimality.

relationships: Uses the journal criterion's exact certificate, overlap, respectful-assignment and local-satisfiability conventions; the new proof bounds its parameter ceiling rather than repeating the private-coefficient failure.
Retains the checked Boolean-function immunity criterion and the separately stronger assignment-indicator theorem, with the manuscript/version distinction.
The certificate stays a constant fraction below the moving half-variable target; this limits one source of its hypothesis, not the correctness of the budget lemma.
The quarter-variable certificate cannot establish the moving near-half-variable old-PC hypothesis.
